newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa 96/97 average wheat price up 13.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa 96/97 average wheat price up 13.5 pct.

text.p: South Africa's Wheat Board said on Friday the average minimum selling price for wheat (free-on-rail) in the 1996/97 season will be 1,032 rand a tonne -- a 13.5 percent increase on the previous season.
Although the selling price was originally to be based on wheat import parity, the Board said it was agreed that a minimum price be set as a "safety net" if import parity was below the level of 1,032.
It said import parity as calculated on October 1 was in fact below this minimum price.

The Board said net producer delivery prices for wheat in the southern area would be 894.26 rand per tonne, 14 percent up on last season. Producer delivery prices in the remaining areas would be 909.44 rand per tonne -- up 13.3 percent.
South Africa is expecting a wheat crop of 2.571 million tonnes this season, up from 1.969 million last year.
